item.title: Baton Rouge Weather: The warming trend continues
item.description: BATON ROUGE, La. (Louisiana First) — We are entering a long stretch of very warm weather across south Louisiana and southwest Mississippi. TONIGHT: Overnight lows will be in the mid and lower 50s. Winds will begin to transition to more out of the south-southeast as high pressure clears the area. Patchy fog will likely develop [...]

item.title: 1 dead after shooting Friday night in Baton Rouge
item.description: A 42-year-old man, Jermaine Clark, was shot and killed in Baton Rouge, Louisiana on Friday, February 27.

item.title: Man sentenced in Baton Rouge shooting that killed pregnant woman
item.description: Suspect in April 2023 shooting of pregnant woman pleads guilty to manslaughter and feticide, sentenced to 30 years in prison.

item.title: Trail system to honor Baton Rouge's role in shaping civil rights movement
item.description: Baton Rouge is officially marking its place in civil rights history.

item.title: Shield of Hope Gala supports Baton Rouge Salvation Army
item.description: The Salvation Army of Greater Baton Rouge is hosting its annual Shield of Hope Gala on March 19th to raise funds for local programs, featuring music, food, and a silent auction.

item.title: Victim identified in deadly shooting on Osage Street
item.description: A man was killed in an early morning shooting in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, after a fight, and the suspect fled the scene.

item.title: This Week in Louisiana Politics: Tax reforms and the Senate race
item.description: Louisiana families are receiving larger refunds this tax season due to the implementation of the largest income tax cut in state history, which includes a flat 3% personal income tax rate, increased standard deductions, and doubled retirement income exemptions.

item.title: Louisiana lawmakers respond to U.S. strikes on Iran
item.description: Louisiana officials have released statements in response to the U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran, with Rep. Julia Letlow (R) and Rep. Steve Scalise (R) expressing support for the strikes, while Rep. Troy Carter (D) urging serious consideration and a clear plan for any use of military force.
